requirement_text.REQ-358: Extend the UAT scenario YAML schema with a scope field and step-level `when:` branching (eq/in/else only). Extend UAT-RUNNER/WF-05 docs with an explicit environment target (base URL + credential source). Add a schema-validation mix task rejecting malformed scope/branching scenario files with a clear error. Backward compatible: every existing scenario file still parses and its non-branching behavior is unchanged. The branching construct must be proven sufficient for a login-routing example (role=PLATFORM_ADMIN / role=<tenant-role> / unauthenticated, three distinct outcomes).

Continue to the full procedure.

Write test/specs/REQ-358.md (requirement text, test cases, why each exists) and ExUnit test code under test/letflow/ (e.g. test/letflow/mix_tasks/check_uat_scenario_schema_test.exs) exercising lib/mix/tasks/letflow.check_uat_scenario_schema.ex's pure core functions directly (not by shelling out to `mix` — call the module's public functions, per this project's existing mix-task test convention, e.g. check lib/mix/tasks/letflow.check_requirements_registration.ex's own test file if one exists as a precedent for how this project tests mix tasks). Cover:
1. AC1 (schema backward compatibility): a fixture derived from an existing real scenario file (or the actual file itself) with no `scope:`/`branches:` fields validates successfully, deriving `scope` from `company_id` per the design's default-derivation rule.
2. AC2 (malformed rejection): at least one deliberately malformed scope/branching fixture (bad `scope:` type, unknown `when:` operator, missing `else` at the end of a `branches:` list, etc. — pick concrete cases from the design doc's SCHEMA-1..6 rules) is rejected with a specific, checkable error.
3. AC4 (branching sufficiency): a test asserting the throwaway login-routing fixture (test/fixtures/uat/scenarios/_throwaway/login-routing-example.yaml, already in artifacts_in) validates successfully against the schema, and ideally a further unit-level test on the branch-evaluation logic itself covering all three named branches (PLATFORM_ADMIN / tenant role / unauthenticated/else) if the mix task's design exposes a testable branch-matching function separate from full-file validation — check the design doc/module for such a function; if none exists (branch evaluation is UAT-RUNNER's own runtime job, not something the mix task does), state that explicitly rather than inventing a fake test.

Do NOT write a test asserting anything about UAT-RUNNER's own runtime branch evaluation against a live role/session — that is not unit-testable (UAT-RUNNER is a Claude subagent reading markdown procedurally against a real HTTP session, not an Elixir function), and REQ-358's AC3/AC4 require a REAL UAT-RUNNER run against QA for that half, which is a separate step this run will dispatch later (not TEST-DESIGNER's job). Do not fake this with an ExUnit test that doesn't exercise anything real — this project's own anti-over-engineering/no-manufactured-busywork norm applies.

Every acceptance criterion must have at least one test case that would fail if violated — verify this by reasoning through each test against a hypothetical broken implementation, not just asserting it.
